Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a significant increase in p95 latency and a spike in 5xx errors across our inference calls this morning (around 09:30 UTC). This coincides with the v3.1b model variant and the new qprofile that was pushed to our route in the deployment window last night.

Impact: 10-15% of requests return 500/502 within the first token; p95 has jumped from ~120ms to ~680ms. Customer-facing features are timing out.

We've attached a filtered log bundle and a short HAR for a failed request. Can your team confirm whether the v3.1b quant profile is known to exhibit decode stalls on longer prompts? We need an urgent mitigation plan and, if needed, a rollback.

Attachments: rallypoint-error-log-20260521.zip (zip)

Thanks,
Sandeep Rao

On Fri, May 21, 2026 at 03:28 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonas and Priyom, please triage kernel logs and KV cache metrics.

Quick tech summary from initial triage:
- Repro: the provided HAR reproduces a decode stall on longer sequences (~>512 tokens) when served against v3.1b with the new qprofile. Short prompts and embeddings are unaffected.
- Error mode: a subset of requests hit a token-level timeout inside the attention kernel; we see long stalls followed by internal worker exits that surface as 502 to the client.
- Batching: We observed higher-than-expected batching collisions due to the new tokenization alignment in v3.1b — this increased per-request latency under medium traffic.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Rapid traffic split to v3.1a (pre-quant) for 100% of production traffic for the next 2 hours while we roll forward a patch. Pros: fastest way to restore p95. Cons: temporary regression in cost.
2) Canary rollback of qprofile only (keep v3.1b weights, revert quant params) across 20% -> 100% with health checks. Pros: lower cost delta. Cons: still requires careful canarying; might not address token-level stalls.
3) Apply a temporary token-timeout bypass/hard-retry for stalled kernels and route to fallback replicas after 2500ms. Pros: no variant swap; Cons: could increase error counts and load.

We recommend option 1 for customer-facing traffic while we push a patched qprofile (expected 6–12 hours). I will prepare the rollback playbook and can execute with Marissa's sign-off.

Attachments: short trace snippets included inline (see attached logs). (attachment: none)

Summary: Our engineers have identified the regression root cause as an alignment issue in the v3.1b qprofile that increases batching collisions and leads to intermittent token-level stalls on longer prompts.

Proposed immediate action (needs your approval):
- At 09:30 UTC we will re-route 100% of your production inference traffic to v3.1a (the immediate warm fallback). This is expected to restore p95 within 10–15 minutes.
- While traffic is on v3.1a we will apply a patched qprofile to v3.1b in staging and run a 2-hour canary before reintroducing.
- If you prefer, we can instead do a qprofile-only rollback; we recommend full variant switch for speed.
